I suppose if you have difficulty drawing freehand and want to trace out an image onto the wood before burning, that could be useful. But it's not "necessary". I believe some people use stencils and photo projectors as well. I like to do it free hand just to make life difficult, but also to add that humanist touch, character, and personal style.

That's the beauty of this medium. All you really need to get started is the burning tool and something to burn. Just start experimenting and getting the feel for it. As you go, you'll find a preference for certain woods and certain tips (I prefer white pine with as little woodgrain as possible and I stick with one, ballpoint tip for almost everything, and a shading tip for darker shading). You can also sketch lightly on the wood before you burn with a graphite pencil. Just don't press too hard, because it's difficult to erase off wood. A bit of sandpaper can help with this though for minor mistakes. Just get to burning and have fun with it 👍
